feat(bunna): verify Bunna Bank receipt links and QR codes (beta)

Bunna receipt links (online.bunnabanksc.com/receipt/#/{token}) open an
Angular app that sends the fragment token to
online.bunnabanksc.com/st_backend/api/v1/advice?data={token}. No credential.
The receipt page draws its QR as online.bunnabanksc.com/#/receipt-v2/{token}.

- parser bunna: opaque base64 token (16-256 bytes, round-trip checked);
  SUCCESS envelope maps payer/receiver (Bunna's own account mask kept, an
  unmasked account is masked), amount, date-only tranDate, tranId;
  fee/total fields (all 0.0 upstream) left unmapped; FAILURE is "not
  confirmed" with checkedUrl, never fake
- url-detector: exact host, #/{token}, #/receipt/{token}, #/receipt-v2/{token},
  segments joined like Bunna's router; feedback and other paths ignored
- reference-case: canonicalBunnaToken (URL-decode, space->+, base64url,
  padding) so link, QR and pasted token share one cache key
- gate: bunna is an opaque lookup key
- manifest: live + beta, format bunna-advice-json, endpoint docs, health
  probe on an all-zero token expecting the FAILURE envelope
- tests with synthetic data only

fix(sdk): send lowercase receipt references in the bank's form

getReceiptUrl / get_receipt_url / GetReceiptURL in all five SDKs send
a CBE FT reference, Dashen FT Ref or ZamZam id that only differs from
the bank's format by case, spaces or dashes in that format, as the
server reads it. A CBE Receipt ID keeps its case. New shared
receiptUrlCases fixtures cover it. verify needs no change: it sends the
reference as given and the server normalises it.

Python's deprecated direct mode applies the same rule as the server.

feat(verify): show references in capitals and hint after a not-found

The form shows a typed reference the way the bank prints it when the
field loses focus or the check starts (not for a mixed-case token on a
guessed bank, which may be a case-sensitive CBE Receipt ID). Detection,
the account field and the official Telebirr/M-Pesa link use the same
canonical form.

When the bank has no such receipt, or rejects the reference, and what
was typed had lowercase letters, spaces or dashes or not the bank's
usual shape, the card adds one line: references are usually capitals
and digits; scan the QR or paste the link, or copy it exactly.

A lowercase apps.cbe.com.et link is read too. Tests cover each
case-insensitive bank and the case-sensitive tokens left alone.

fix(verify): accept lowercase references for uppercase-only banks

One shared rule (src/lib/reference-case.ts) gives each bank's typed
reference its canonical form: trimmed, spaces and dashes dropped when that
gives the bank's shape, and uppercased for CBE FT references, BOA,
Telebirr, M-Pesa, Dashen and CBE Birr. The verifier applies it before the
format is picked, so POST /api/verify, the batch route, the CLI and every
SDK get it; /api/receipt and the cache key use the same rule.

References read out of a link or QR are uppercased but never compacted.
CBE Receipt IDs, Awash and eBirr share tokens, ZamZam ids and the Telebirr
QR payload keep their case.

CRC-16/CCITT-FALSE), a Python decoder, and why a valid QR is not proof
of payment. Synthetic examples only (ABC1D2E3F4, XKJ0L9N8M7).

Linked from the Telebirr bank page's QR section, the CBE, BOA and
receipt-formats guides, the /guides index (For developers), llms.txt and
docs/telebirr-qr.md. Tests check the guide's sample QR and CRCs against

docs: SDK retries, batch chunking, beta/orderId, Python extras, release flow

- Root README, every SDK README, /docs and /developers describe the new

- PHP README: PHP 8.1+, 1.5.0 changes, and why the older breaking changes

- docs/RELEASING.md: release PR (--files-only) then --tag-only on main,

  bad version (npm deprecate / PyPI yank need the owners' credentials).

release: registry check, loud publish, PR-friendly bump-version, wider CI matrix

publish.yml:
- A registry that already has the version now FAILS the job on the first
  run (npm, GitHub Packages, PyPI used to skip silently, which is how the
  June 1.4.1 builds stayed on npm/PyPI while main moved on). Only a re-run
  (run_attempt > 1) skips, with a notice.
- PyPI: twine check --strict, and the wheel must ship LICENSE and need only
  requests/urllib3 at runtime. npm/PyPI: the tag must equal the package
  version. Packagist: scripts/check-php-dist.sh before the update call.
- New verify-registries job (needs every publish job, runs even if one
  failed): scripts/check-registries.mjs polls npm, PyPI, Packagist p2,
  pub.dev, the Go proxy and GitHub Packages for up to 10 minutes and fails
  unless all serve the version, Packagist and the Go proxy from the tagged
  commit. Also runnable by hand: node scripts/check-registries.mjs 1.5.0.

scripts/bump-version.sh:
- --files-only X.Y.Z rewrites the version lines on any branch (release PR);

feat: smart fallback for geo-blocked banks (Telebirr, M-Pesa)

When verification fails for geo-blocked banks, cheki now shows a smart
fallback panel with two paths:

1. Copy & Paste (mobile-first, zero setup):
   - User opens the receipt page in their browser (Ethiopian IP)
   - Selects all text, copies, pastes into cheki's textarea
   - cheki parses the pasted content server-side

2. Bookmarklet (desktop, one-time setup):
   - User drags the bookmarklet to their bookmarks bar
   - Opens any Telebirr/M-Pesa receipt page, clicks the bookmarklet
   - Bookmarklet reads page HTML, sends to /api/parse, shows overlay

The /api/parse endpoint now auto-detects content type (HTML, JSON, or
plain text) and wraps plain text in minimal HTML so parser validation
checks pass. Returns full parsed receipt with all Telebirr-specific fields.

feat: fallback 'Open Receipt' button for geo-blocked banks

When our server can't reach telebirr/mpesa (cloud IPs blocked),
we return the receipt URL so the user can open it directly in
their browser. Their browser uses their own Ethiopian IP, which
the bank accepts. Three-tier fallback:
1. Direct IP + X-Forwarded-For (works when self-hosted in ET)
2. Edge runtime proxy (Cloudflare network, different IPs)
3. Fallback URL for client-side open (user's browser/IP)
